Welcome to Hillingdon Manor School
As Headteacher of Hillingdon Manor School, I am delighted to welcome you to our community. We are excited to have you join us and look forward to supporting you on your educational journey.
Hillingdon Manor is an independent specialist school for autistic pupils aged 11 to 19. Spread across two vibrant sites, we offer a personalised, autism-specific education that nurtures the unique strengths and abilities of every pupil. Through our adapted curriculum, we ensure that each individual’s needs are fully met, enabling them to achieve their full potential both in education and in life.
Our school community is built on our core values: Ready, Respectful and Safe. These principles guide everything we do and help create a positive, supportive learning environment where every student can thrive.
We also actively promote British Values—democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect—preparing our pupils to be thoughtful, responsible citizens in today’s diverse society. Our curriculum encourages a broad understanding of public services, institutions, and the voluntary sector in England, while fostering the life skills needed to distinguish right from wrong.
We are truly excited to welcome you to Hillingdon Manor School and look forward to working in partnership with you and your family to ensure the very best outcomes for every pupil.
Warm regards, Grace Mullally Headteacher, Hillingdon Manor School & The Courtyard

KS4 Pupils Work Experience at HMS
Some of our pupils recently took part in a Duke of Edinburgh (DoE) Work Experience session with Mick, helping to set up furniture in the staff room. Throughout the activity, pupils demonstrated a range of valuable transferable skills, including teamwork, communication, problem-solving, initiative, and resilience, as they worked together to complete practical tasks in a real workplace environment.
Work experience is a key part of our Careers Education programme, helping pupils develop an understanding of different workplaces, employment opportunities, and the skills needed for future success. Through experiences such as these, learners gain valuable insight into the world of work, enabling them to make more informed decisions about their future pathways. It was fantastic to see pupils engaging so positively and confidently in this meaningful learning opportunity.

Home Parents and Carers
Parents & Carers
The parents and carers of the children and young people we educate and care for are so important, and we take care to give them all the expert ongoing support they need at every stage of their partnership with us.
From the moment they make their first enquiry and right through the child or young person’s time in one of our schools or residential homes, we’re there for them with tailored advice and support.
Tune in to Autism Unpacked, where we’re navigating SEN together through honest conversations, expert insight, lived experience and practical advice.
We’re joined by professionals from education and therapy, alongside parents, carers and people with lived experience, to share practical insights, explore the topics that matter and help families and those supporting children and young people feel better informed.
© OFG Education 2026

Home Parents and Carers Important Information
Important Information
We work closely with parents, carers, and other stakeholders to ensure that students’ targets and outcomes are met.
Before all students start, we ensure they have time to transition from school or other providers and complete a statement of need and baseline assessment.
Parent/ carer contact is crucial, and we ensure through various methods that parents are informed of progress through telephone calls, half termly reports and regular information.
We also work closely with local authorities to ensure that Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) procedures are followed, and all appropriate parties are invited to EHCP annual reviews for input and contribution.

Home Parents and Carers Referrals and admissions
Referrals and admissions
Criteria for Admission to Hillingdon Manor School
Procedures for Admission of Pupils
Parents may visit the school on designated open mornings.
The most effective route for admission is when parents and the Local Authority agree that HMS may be an appropriate placement for a child and a joint application is made for assessment.
This involves the Local Authority contacting the school to request an assessment to determine whether HMS would be an appropriate placement for the child.
The child and parents would then attend an Initial Contact Meeting at the school. The parent would bring a copy of the most recent reports (where possible) from the previous education provider to inform the meeting.
The school will then offer an assessment process, which is tailored to the young person’s individual needs. Following this assessment, the school’s referral and assessment team will meet to review the assessment. The Local Authority and parents will then be notified of the outcome of assessment via an assessment report.
If the school decides that it can meet the child’s Special Educational Needs and there is a suitable place available, the Local Authority will be asked to confirm that it accepts financial responsibility for the placement for the admission process to continue.
Following confirmation that the Local Authority will accept financial responsibility for the placement, a Transition Plan is developed by HMS in consultation with the child’s parents, current school staff and other relevant professionals. Transition Plans are tailored to the individual needs of the pupil and include social stories to prepare the child for new routines and staff. A start date will be mutually agreed with HMS, the local authority and parents.
© OFG Education 2026

Home About Us What we do
What We Do
Hillingdon Manor School is a specialist school for children and young people aged 11-19 years, who have been diagnosed with Autistic Spectrum Conditions (ASC).
Hillingdon Manor School opened in 1999 as an independent school with the aim of providing a tailored learning environment for children and young people with autism.
The school offers a unique mix of education and support to pupils within a wide spectrum of needs and abilities. Personalised teaching and learning in an autism specific environment allows pupils’ individual needs to be addressed completely and their capabilities fully realised.
The Manor – Secondary
Our school, located in Hillingdon, caters for children aged 11 to 19 years old. Hillingdon Manor School is located across two sites – The Manor and The Courtyard – where we have provision for Year 7 up to Year 14, covering Key Stage 3, 4 and 5. Our Key Stage 3 cohort are set across the two sites, where cross-site learning takes place. The Manor site exclusively offers the extension of Key Stage 4 and 5 learning.
All students are supported to learn at their own level through personalised teaching and differentiated lessons based on the National Curriculum. The school is proud to offer students access to a range of excellent educational opportunities, certified subjects and national accreditations, as well as vocational and life skills subjects to prepare pupils for life beyond school.
To find out more about the Secondary Site and the Curriculum, please see here.

HMS Pupils Take Part in Kindness Assembly
On Friday 18th September 2026, pupils took part in a special Kindness Assembly, where they explored the importance of showing kindness, empathy, and respect to others.
Following the assembly, pupils continued the learning in their classrooms through a range of engaging activities focused on how they can demonstrate kindness in their everyday lives. From thoughtful discussions to creative tasks, pupils reflected on the positive impact that small acts of kindness can have on both individuals and the wider school community.
It was wonderful to see so many pupils embracing the message and finding meaningful ways to spread kindness throughout the school. Thank you to Claire Stapleton, Deputy Headteacher, for overseeing this event.

Careers Education
Welcome to Careers Education at Hillingdon Manor School.
Links to important documents related to our Career Programme: Careers Programme 2026-2027
Our curriculum focusses on careers, and we provide our students with meaningful career-related opportunities and activities throughout their time at Hillingdon Manor School.
We are always looking to improve our provision and welcome feedback from students, parents, and carers. If you would like to give feedback, please click here: Parent Carer or Student Feedback
Provider Access Policy
We welcome the opportunity to welcome employers, Further Education settings and Training Providers into our School. Are you interested in being a partner with Hillingdon Manor School? If you would like to enquire about offering work experience placements or student talks and mentoring, or showcasing your setting to our students, please do get in touch, we would love to discuss this with you! To do so, please contact Mitzi Smith, the EHCP & Transition Officer who works closely with OFG’s Future Programme in sharing information from student’s Transition Plans in order to the Futures Team to support the development of careers opportunities for our students as well as providing careers advice to our students yearly.
Thank you for your time, we are always looking to improve our provision and welcome feedback from training providers and employers if you would like to give feedback please click here: Training Provider or Employer Feedback
Marcel Balaban – Careers Lead
Marcel leads on all aspects of Careers Education at Hillingdon Manor School, including planning the careers curriculum; organising real life and tailored opportunities for pupils across the Key Stages appropriate to age and stage of development; delivering staff CPD; and ensuring the school is fully compliant with the Gatesby Benchmark. Marcel oversees all aspects of Work Experience, ensuring our pupils have exposure to the world of work.
Mitzi Smith – EHCP & Transition Coordinator
Mitzi leads on all aspects of Key Stage transfers, and preparations for pupil’s transition to new settings, including Further and Higher Education, apprenticeships and work. Mitzi works alongside the Careers Lead, Marcel, and our SENCo, Laura, to ensure pupils have the skills and experiences necessary to be successful in life after Hillingdon Manor.
